attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No valid locality-extraction theorem maps arbitrary small circuits for H_N into one-sided formula-local separator covers with subthreshold overhead.
steps: Assume a circuit C of size S<N^{1+epsilon} computes H_N exactly.
Try to cover positive inputs x by choosing a witness position j with SAT(G_N(x,j)).
Attempt to define a local predicate P_{j,C} on y=G_N(x,j) that is one-sided sound and accepts enough chosen witnesses.
The only available predicate from C is global: it depends on x and on correlations among all generated positions, not on y alone.
DNF expansion of C gives global accepting regions on x, but conversion to formula-local predicates can cost 2^S or require inverting G_N.
A planted-control carrier makes the obstruction exact: H_N=b_N is easy, while local formula labels may remain separator-hard.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The separator machinery proves only upper-bound falsifiers. It does not prove arbitrary circuit lower bounds, so it cannot yet support the target-preserving SAT notin P/poly consequence.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: normal-form extraction gate

assumptions: Circuit size is nonuniform Boolean size on the N-bit carrier input.
Local separator predicates see one generated formula and its position, not the whole carrier input x.
Error sets of size E are patchable by equality gates at cost O(EN).
The planted-control construction is a formal falsifier in oracle or pseudorandom-label models unless a SAT-specific anti-control certificate is added.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j in [M]} SAT(G_N(x,j)) on N input bits, with M=N^q, query length L=(log N)^d, and shared generator circuit size N^rho.
target object: SAT notin P/poly, obtained only through the contrapositive substitution bridge from SAT circuits on length L to circuits for H_N.
controlled interface: shared generated-OR substitution where all SAT calls have length L and the entire query list is produced with size N^rho without position-specific advice.

target-preserving condition: q<1+epsilon, rho<1+epsilon, d>1, and every conversion of a source upper bound to a target consequence preserves nonuniform circuit size and the exact N^{1+epsilon} threshold.
Sep_N^{1s}(K,s,E) means K position-indexed predicates of size at most s, sound on the generated universe, hitting all but E positive bags.
A planted-control carrier has a simple bit b_N(x) such that b_N=1 forces at least one generated satisfiable formula and b_N=0 forces all generated formulas unsatisfiable.

candidate_lemmas.statement: One-sided formula-local separator covers are a valid sufficient falsifier for the generated-OR source lower bound, but they are not a necessary normal form for arbitrary circuits computing H_N unless a new locality-extraction theorem is proved.

assumptions: The extraction must preserve q,rho,d,epsilon and cannot add advice depending on individual positions beyond the shared generator.
The separator family must be one-sided sound on all generated negative bags, not merely on a sampled distribution.
The conversion must avoid natural-proof leakage: a dense, constructive separator-hardness property for SAT truth tables would be barrier-suspect.
definitions: locality-extraction hypothesis: from any size-S circuit C deciding H_N, construct Sep_N^{1s}(K,s,E) with K(s+L^{O(1)})+EN <= S polylog N.
normal-form gap: arbitrary circuits may compute global correlations in x without yielding any local predicate on generated formulas.
barrier status: such an extraction theorem must be nonrelativizing and SAT-specific; the target substitution bridge itself relativizes.

The global bit b_N is computable by size O(N) circuits.

separator demand: a local predicate must accept generated positives and reject all generated negatives without seeing b_N(x).

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no canonical target-preserving identity between the annihilator polynomial extracted from H_v and the SAT_m truth table. The arithmetic source lower bound can be completely disjoint from the Boolean target language.
steps: Fix an explicit H_v hitting all nonzero F-arithmetic circuits of size s(v) and syntactic degree d(v).
Use linear algebra: if r^v>|H_v|, choose a nonzero annihilator P_H of individual degree <r that vanishes on H_v.
If v(r-1)<=d(v), the hitting-set property implies P_H has arithmetic circuit size greater than s(v). This is a valid arithmetic lower bound.
Try to infer SAT_m notin SIZE(m^k) by assuming a Boolean circuit C for SAT_m and translating C into an arithmetic circuit for P_H.
The translation fails unless a uniform Phi_m proves that C computes enough of P_H, not just SAT_m, and preserves B(m,k)<=s(v), D(m,k)<=d(v).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The route proves only P_H notin arithmetic-size s. It does not rule out polynomial Boolean circuits for SAT, and a BGS collapse oracle is a falsifier for any relativizing final implication.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: arithmetic PIT target gate

assumptions: The field F, variable count v, size threshold s, and syntactic-degree threshold d are fixed before seeing a putative SAT circuit.
H_v is explicit enough for the intended construction, but explicitness alone does not identify P_H with SAT_m.
The hitting-set statement is for arithmetic circuits, while the target lower bound is for Boolean circuits on m input bits.
The interface Phi_m must be uniform and target-preserving; otherwise a valid arithmetic lower bound remains irrelevant to P vs NP.
definitions: source object: an F-arithmetic hitting set H_v for v-variate circuits of size s(v) and syntactic degree d(v), together with a nonzero low-degree annihilator P_H satisfying P_H|_{H_v}=0.
target object: the Boolean truth-table family SAT_m and the nonuniform lower bound SAT_m notin SIZE(m^k), not merely an arithmetic VP/VNP or NEXP consequence.

controlled interface: a uniform map Phi_m sending any Boolean circuit for SAT_m of size m^k to an F-arithmetic circuit computing the named source polynomial or its evaluation table, with bounded size B(m,k) and degree D(m,k).
target-preserving condition: B(m,k)<=s(v) and D(m,k)<=d(v), with no hidden advice, large-constant encoding, oracle leakage, or padding change between the SAT slice and the source polynomial.

Without that simulator the route is a target mismatch, not P != NP progress.

The BGS oracle A with P^A=NP^A is available as a route falsifier.
A nonrelativizing argument is not disqualified, but it must name the exact nonrelativizing bridge.

target model: relativized Boolean classes P^O and NP^O.
interface: the alleged implication must remain meaningful after adding an arbitrary Boolean oracle to Turing machines.
escape condition: the proof must use a genuinely nonrelativizing target-preserving feature tying SAT syntax to the arithmetic object.

The circuit model can multiply the h linear forms using O(vh) wires or gates.

The annihilator construction is not automatically a Razborov-Rudich natural property over Boolean truth tables; if made poly(N)-constructive and large for SAT truth tables, it must be audited as natural.
Arithmetization is allowed only after naming the nonalgebrizing or syntax-sensitive bridge from SAT to P_H; otherwise the route stays in arithmetic complexity.
The required transfer inequalities are B(m,k)<=s(v) and D(m,k)<=d(v); padding exponent beta can falsify them even when the arithmetic lower bound is valid.

falsifiers: BGS collapse oracle A: P^A=NP^A while the unrelativized arithmetic hitting-set statement can remain valid, falsifying relativizing PIT-to-PNP transfers.

Target-object mismatch: a Boolean circuit for SAT_m need not yield an arithmetic circuit for the annihilator P_H, so the lower bound may concern the wrong function.
Advice leakage: large constants or nonuniform maps Phi_m can encode H_v or the SAT truth table and destroy any valid lower-bound transfer.
Padding collapse: for L_{n,beta}(u,w)=SAT_n(u), the padded length m=n^beta can make claimed thresholds refer to m while the algebraic object only sees the n-bit core.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known non-natural, advice-free, bounded-D certificate proves anti-sparse-correction distance from every unrestricted a-size circuit within the E verifier budget.
steps: Start with the valid extraction invariant from earlier cycles: a kappa-dense, bounded-D, E-canonical source containing an actual row of circuit complexity above 2^{epsilon m} yields E lower-bound exponent delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
Repair the source-side no-gos by replacing zero/one load constraints with the stronger condition that every accepted row is farther than (2^{epsilon m}-a)/(c m) from every circuit of size a.
Use the sparse-correction lemma to prove this condition is necessary for exact MCSP no-side soundness and catches balanced perturbations of parity or majority that previous load tests missed.
Try to define the carrier as a sparse certificate family proving FAR_{a,r}(T) for a=2^{epsilon m-1} and r=Theta(2^{epsilon m}/m).

The naive verifier must compare T with all a-size circuits, costing 2^{Theta(a log a)} rather than 2^{O(m)}; random sampling gives only average-case evidence and can accept an exact sparse patch of a small circuit.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The cycle proves a sharper falsifier for source proposals and preserves the valid carrier-to-E bridge, but it does not construct the hard MCSP row or separate P from NP.

assumptions: Standard fan-in two Boolean circuit model with constants; an equality test to a hardwired m-bit string has size O(m).
The carrier soundness target is exact unrestricted circuit complexity, not correlation hardness or average-case distance.
The accepted row is used as a truth table at input length m, with no advice-dependent choice of the exceptional set.
definitions: source object: a length-m MCSP carrier cell A_{m,z} of truth tables T:{0,1}^m->{0,1}, produced by a uniform short-certificate verifier and intended to contain only no-instances at threshold s(m)=2^{epsilon m}.
target object: an unrestricted Boolean circuit lower bound C(T)>2^{epsilon m} for a row used by the carrier-to-E extraction, later yielding E lower bounds after kappa,D losses.
controlled interface: compare each accepted table with every small base circuit g and account for exact sparse corrections by equality tests on exceptional inputs.

target-preserving condition: the verifier must guarantee distance from every a-size base circuit exceeds (2^{epsilon m}-a)/(c m); otherwise the accepted row has a small unrestricted circuit and the MCSP no-side claim is invalid.

If an accepted MCSP carrier row T differs from some circuit g of size a on t inputs and a+cmt<s(m), then T has unrestricted circuit size below s(m). Hence any valid no-side carrier at threshold 2^{epsilon m} must be far from every small base circuit by more than the exact sparse-patch radius, not merely balanced away from 0 and 1.

The patch list is nonuniformly hardwired into the target circuit, so uniform obscurity of the verifier does not help soundness.

The desired parameters are a around 2^{epsilon m-1} and r around 2^{epsilon m}/m.
The carrier verifier budget is 2^{O(m)} with O(m)-length certificates or E-canonical unranking.
